title: openai-compat: support Responses API variants, seed/determinism and metadata passthrough
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: The OpenAI Responses family exposes newer fields (seed, determinism flags, and richer metadata) that our OpenAI-compatible layer did not fully surface. This caused two customer issues: 1) seed/determinism not being honored end-to-end leading to surprising non-deterministic outputs for customers who set seed; 2) user-provided metadata being dropped when requests were proxied through the compat layer, breaking downstream observability and auditing. This PR updates the compat adapter and SDK mappings so Responses variants behave like OpenAI's responses endpoints for seed, deterministic settings, streaming, function/tool-calling payloads, and metadata passthrough. Checklist: - [x] Propagate seed and determinism flags from compat API to internal inference request path - [x] Preserve user metadata fields (top-level and response-level) through request/response roundtrips - [x] Stabilize streaming path and fix reassembly bug for chunked function call args - [x] Update Python/TS SDK parameter mappings and add tests - [x] Add regression tests and an e2e using the responses-compat fixture - [x] Update docs and release notes
  Changes in this PR are intentionally scoped to the compat adapter, SDK shims, routing layer annotations, and tests. No model runtime kernels were changed. The adapter ensures backward compatibility with existing OpenAI-compat clients and introduces feature parity for the newer Responses fields.
commits_summary: 3 commits: initial adapter changes to surface seed/determinism; streaming reassembly + function-calling fix; tests/docs and SDK parameter mapping updates
review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Please confirm that seed is propagated to both cached and cold-start code paths. Asha: confirmed and added a unit test for KV cache paths.

Diego Morales: Streaming reassembly looked fragile; can we simplify the state machine? Asha: refactored streaming_relay to use a small deterministic buffer and added comments + tests for chunk boundary cases.
June Park: Docs need a migration note for SDK users. Asha: added a migration subsection with example parameter mappings for Python/TS.
Diego Morales (approve): LGTM after addressing streaming test flakiness. Liam O'Connor (approve): Verified e2e against responses-compat fixture. June Park (approve): Docs and release notes look good.
ci_checks_summary: CI summary: build: pass; unit tests: pass; integration tests: pass; lint: pass; e2e: initially flaky on CI (streaming fixture timeout) -> rerun passed. Coverage: +1.2% on openai_compat module. All checks green on final run.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash by June Park. Merge strategy: squash merge to keep adapter change cohesive. Rollout: staged to canary (5% of traffic) for 24h, then 100% after monitoring; no rollback required.
release_notes: OpenAI-compat: Added full Responses API variant support in the compat adapter. Seed and determinism flags are now honored and propagated to the inference path; user metadata is preserved end-to-end. Streaming stability fixes for chunked function-calling payloads. SDKs (Python/TS) updated to expose seed/determinism parameters and match Responses semantics. Backwards compatible; no breaking changes.
notes_for_ops: Canary notes: when enabling canary, watch tokenization/latency P95 and the responses_stream_chunk_errors metric. If streaming reassembly errors exceed baseline by >0.1%, rollback the compat adapter version. Added a temporary feature flag openai_compat.resp_v2_canary to toggle behavior per region.
testing_summary: Added unit tests for seed propagation and KV cache path, streaming reassembly unit tests including chunk boundaries, and an end-to-end test using a small deterministic model fixture. Local manual validation performed with python SDK and TS SDK examples. QA ran the responses e2e against SUP-724 reproducer case and confirmed metadata passthrough and deterministic outputs when seed is set.
risk_assessment: Low: changes limited to compat adapter, SDK shims, and routing middleware. Mitigations: feature flag for staged rollout, automated regression tests, and monitoring on responses_stream_chunk_errors and openai_compat.request_mismatch metrics.
authors_notes: Follow-ups: 1) evaluate exposing a top-level "deterministic" convenience parameter at the Redwood API layer; 2) canonicalize metadata field names across integrations; 3) small perf sweep on streaming_relay buffer sizing if P95 increases under load.
